questions.q: True or false? The pivot checks both shoulders before the ball arrives.
questions.explain: Right, it's true: checking both shoulders shows the pivot where the marker is and where the room is.
choiceExplanations: Right, it's true: checking both shoulders shows the pivot where the marker is and where the room is.
The pivot looks first, so they already know whether to turn or lay the ball off.

questions.q: The pivot wants to turn left. In which picture is there room?
questions.explain: Yes. The marker is on the right, so the left side is free to turn into.
choiceExplanations: The marker is on the left side, so a left turn runs straight into them.
Yes. The marker is on the right, so the left side is free to turn into.

questions.q: The marker covers the turn, and the right ala is marked. Which lay-off is best?
options: Lay off to the right ala
Lay off to the left ala
questions.explain: Yes. The left ala is free with a clear lane, so the lay-off keeps the ball.
choiceExplanations: A defender stands in the lane to the right ala, so that lay-off gets cut out.

questions.q: The PIVOT has room behind. Which move turns with the ball close?
options: Drag-back: sole on top, pull it and turn
questions.explain: Yes. The sole pulls the ball back under your body, so you turn with it close.
choiceExplanations: A toe poke is a shot; it does not turn you.
A nutmeg goes through a defender's legs; here you need to turn.
Yes. The sole pulls the ball back under your body, so you turn with it close.
